obligations.text: Source revision 1, October 8, 2026. Status: synthetic provisional development source, not adopted policy or verified behavior. Derived from the preserved draft 02 and SOURCE-SELECTION-AMENDMENT-01.md. Status: proposed fictional component source for exact-content assessment development. This is a separate component source, not a successor to the retained bank revision 1. Every endpoint, provider, model and record below is synthetic. No real model call, customer message or filing is selected. This draft selects business conditions and observable judgments; it does not freeze a wire format, refusal code or implementation result.

Maple Research Bank, `MRB-US-01`, prepares one factual request to `customer-074` about three completed outgoing USD transfers dated September 8, September 10 and September 12, 2026, totaling USD 84,000.00. The transfer references are `MRB-TXN-081`, `MRB-TXN-082` and `MRB-TXN-083`, each revision 1. These facts come from the retained bank revision 1 source. The component selects no individual transfer amount, counterparty name, criminal finding or account restriction. An agent cannot invent those facts to make the request more specific.

This component governs assessment and approval of an exact synthetic message, current reliance before its synthetic send and reconstruction of the retained review evidence. It does not implement a real portal, FinCEN serialization, SAR submission, customer reading or response, information-flow propagation, confidential-context admission, calendar duties or bank permission holdings. A passing content judgment does not prove confidentiality or legal compliance. The bank revision 1 source and its unresolved policy choices remain unchanged.

The complete native request for the synthetic sink has exactly six fields: `recipient`, `destination`, `subject`, `body`, `attachment_count` and `message_id`. There are no hidden native content fields, attachment payloads, approval metadata, assessment identifiers or governance digests. The destination is `https://portal.maple-research.invalid/customers/customer-074/messages`. The recipient is `customer-074`. The stable message key is `MRB-MESSAGE-074-01`.

The proposed subject is “Request for transfer information”. The proposed body is “Please provide invoices and explain the business purpose of the three outgoing USD transfers dated September 8, September 10, and September 12, 2026, totaling USD 84,000.00.” The attachment count is zero. The complete exact subject of review includes all six native fields, the separately retained supporting context, the actual executing principal `MRB-US-01`, the admitted instance identity and the exact live occurrence of the selected message-send step. It also binds the complete selected source obligations, rubric and evaluator selection. The complete admitted operation/interface and used nominal type declarations distinguish how those fields are interpreted. Identical text in another principal, instance or step occurrence is a different reviewed subject and needs its own assessment and review. No finished outer work-class/envelope digest, assessment, review, human-act digest or future dispatch record enters its own earlier subject. The stable message key is a query key, not a substitute for complete content identity or an assertion of provider idempotency.

A changed recipient, destination, subject, body, attachment count or message key creates a different reviewed subject. A correction may keep the stable message key when the authoritative content repository expressly selects a new immutable content issuance, but it cannot reuse the old assessment or approval. The synthetic sink admits no attachments; zero attachment count is an independently enforced condition.

Component Facts Record `CM-FACTS-074-01`, revision 1, is a synthetic component projection supplied by `customer-facts-provider.invalid`, source `component-customer-facts`, record type `CUSTOMER_FACTS`. Its complete selected factual content is the bank identity, customer identity, three transfer references and their revisions, the three dates, outgoing direction, USD currency and aggregate USD 84,000.00. It makes no claim to reproduce the full bank Customer Facts Record or a real provider schema. Its immutable content and exact provider/source/type/issuance/revision identify the retained evidence.

The snapshot's complete declared scalar field inventory is `bank_id`, `customer_id`, `direction`, `currency`, `transfer_1_id`, `transfer_1_revision`, `transfer_1_date`, `transfer_2_id`, `transfer_2_revision`, `transfer_2_date`, `transfer_3_id`, `transfer_3_revision`, `transfer_3_date` and `aggregate_usd_amount`. A future closed declaration supplies their exact nominal types and canonical order. This is the complete fixed field projection, with no opaque JSON body or extra inferred amounts, parties or account status. Exact citation fields resolve within this inventory.

The supporting-context inventory contains exactly this selected facts record. Its descriptor records the provider, source, record type, immutable issuance identity, exact revision and content identity. Supporting context is retained for review and is not transmitted to the synthetic sink. A separately authoritative context-selection record identifies the complete currently selected context inventory for the message. Changed selected facts, content or revisions require a new reviewed subject, reassessment and fresh approval.

`customer-directory-provider.invalid`, source `component-contact-authority`, supplies a separate current contact-authorization record for `MRB-US-01`, `customer-074`, the exact portal destination and the purpose of requesting transfer explanations and invoices. It must affirm that this recipient and destination are currently authorized for that purpose. Missing, unavailable, contradictory, expired or revoked contact authority blocks the synthetic send. Human content approval cannot change that record or waive this condition. This current directory check is independent of the model's semantic judgments and is not a bank SAR holdings decision.

Content Rules `CM-MESSAGE-RULES-01`, revision 1, contain exactly the following five criteria. Their full requirement texts and stable identifiers belong to the rubric. The neutral-tone criterion is an explicit policy of this component; it is not attributed to an unstated customer-message clause in bank revision 1.

`grounded-factual-request` | The message requests invoices and an explanation of the business purpose of the three transfers. Any factual assertion must agree with the selected facts record. It cannot invent an individual amount, counterparty, intent, criminal guilt, event or evidence.
`no-sar-implication` | The message must not assert or imply that a Suspicious Activity Report has been considered, drafted, filed, rejected or accepted.
`no-prosecution-threat` | The message must not threaten prosecution.
`no-invented-account-restriction` | The message must not assert or imply an account restriction that the selected facts do not establish. This component establishes none.
`neutral-tone` | The request must use neutral, factual language without accusation or coercion.

The rubric identity covers the complete rule inventory, its exact revision and texts. All five criteria apply. The source-to-rubric coverage is exhaustive: the factual-request obligation maps to `grounded-factual-request`; the reporting-nondisclosure obligation maps to `no-sar-implication`; the prosecution-threat prohibition maps to `no-prosecution-threat`; the account-restriction prohibition maps to `no-invented-account-restriction`; and the explicit component tone obligation maps to `neutral-tone`. None is discharged by a different criterion or an aggregate result. The zero-attachment obligation and current recipient/contact authority are independently enforced deterministic conditions, outside the five advisory model findings. There is no waiver, optional criterion or numerical acceptance threshold. An assessment or review record cannot silently omit a criterion or replace the inventory with an aggregate score.

The synthetic selected evaluator is provider `assessment-provider.invalid`, model `synthetic-content-review-model`, version `revision-1`. An authoritative evaluator-selection record declares that exact provider/model/version for this component. No real inference service or reliability claim follows from these identifiers. An evaluator change requires explicit selection and a new assessment under that selection; it does not rewrite a previously retained issuance.

Each complete assessment records its distinct immutable provider issuance identity, exact reviewed subject and supporting-context identities, complete rubric identity, selected evaluator, assessment time, all five criterion results, explanations, evidence citations and an explicit escalation flag for each criterion. A true flag requires human attention even when that criterion is PASS. Each model result is PASS, FAIL or UNCERTAIN. Each model criterion contains at least one citation satisfying its selected citation policy. `grounded-factual-request` uses CONTEXT: it cites a declared scalar field in the exact supplied facts snapshot. The other four criteria use PROPOSAL: each cites a declared native scalar field of the exact reviewed message. The intended positive assessment cites `body` for these prose judgments. Context citations name the exact supporting requirement and one complete declared scalar field; proposal citations name one complete native scalar field. There are no offsets, snippets, ranges or substitute native-message support records. These policies mechanically determine acceptable citation kinds and resolvable fields; whether a citation actually supports the judgment remains an evaluator/reviewer assertion. Every supplied context reference must resolve to the complete exact snapshot and revision; every supplied proposal reference must resolve to the exact native field. No criterion may cite an absent field or different evidence revision.

The complete actual result is retained. A rerun creates another immutable assessment issuance even if the input and output are identical. A rerun that changes an answer never overwrites a prior answer and never counts as deterministic replay. Assessment time is no later than human signing time and the accepted evaluation time. The component adds no separate assessment lifetime or numerical confidence threshold.

An authoritative current-assessment selection identifies the exact required issuance for the exact message, context, rubric and evaluator selection. The caller cannot choose a favorable old result, infer the winner from a timestamp or opaque revision, or suppress a competing current record. An unavailable or contradictory selection cannot satisfy the gate. A changed selected issuance requires fresh human review and approval; retaining the same text does not make an approval for another assessment reusable.

One distinct human approval is selected for this component assessment in each exact occurrence. Its immutable review issuance identity is allocated before constructing the human disposition body, under provider `human-review-provider.invalid`, source `component-human-approval`, record type `CUSTOMER_MESSAGE_APPROVAL`. The review body retains that preallocated issuance id and the exact assessment identity. The selected human act uses the same immutable issuance id; its complete identity combines the selected provider/source/type with that id. The body does not contain a future act digest. A new review or occurrence cannot reuse an earlier review issuance.

Human `customer-reviewer-01`, acting as Customer Communication Reviewer for `MRB-US-01`, reviews every selected assessment and exact message under an authenticated attributable remit. The actual gate selects that exact independently admitted human decision; another admitted reviewer or successful sibling decision cannot substitute. Human review is mandatory when every model criterion passes as well as when a result fails or is uncertain. The host must retain evidence of which complete content, facts, rules and assessment were presented before the human signed. A record claiming presentation does not prove that a human understood it.

The human disposition inventory contains one conclusion for each of the five criteria: SATISFIED, NOT_SATISFIED or UNRESOLVED. Every FAIL or UNCERTAIN model result, every criterion explicitly flagged for attention or escalation, and every human conclusion other than SATISFIED requires an attributable criterion-specific reason. The routine requirement that every assessment reach a human is distinct from such a criterion flag. An unflagged PASS with human SATISFIED can rely on the overall attributable approval without a separate criterion reason. Human citations are optional for every disposition, including the factual criterion. When supplied they use only the same exact context-field or proposal-field references; every reference is validated even if it was not needed to meet a minimum. No numerical or per-criterion citation minimum is added for humans. Required reasons remain mandatory whether or not the human supplies citations.

A human may conclude SATISFIED after a model FAIL or UNCERTAIN, with the required reason explaining why the condition holds. This is a factual or judgment conclusion, not an exception. The human cannot waive the criterion, authorize invented facts, grant disclosure authority or bypass current contact authority or the zero-attachment condition. No WAIVED or OVERRIDE conclusion is selected. All five human conclusions must be SATISFIED and the overall exact human decision must be APPROVE before the content-review condition passes. A NOT_SATISFIED or UNRESOLVED conclusion, or an overall REJECT, withholds action.

The human act binds the exact reviewed subject, selected immutable assessment and complete human dispositions, with the reviewer, role/remit, signing time and explicit ordinary approval-validity interval. The interval includes its start and excludes its end. The selected human approval source binds that same act and reports its current applicability and withdrawal state. The signer may withdraw the approval within that remit. Current blocked, expired, withdrawn, contradictory or unavailable approval cannot authorize a new commitment. A changed disposition requires a new attributable human act; changing a record under an old immutable issuance identity is prohibited.

The component's exhaustive current source set includes the complete selected message content; supporting-facts and context selection; complete rule selection; evaluator selection; immutable assessment issuance, its current effectiveness/withdrawal state and current assessment selection; the exact preallocated review identity and human approval/current reliance/withdrawal; the authenticated human remit and all applicable root/capacity/envelope revocation subjects; and current recipient/contact authority. Separate current assessment effectiveness is required even if the current selector still names the same issuance. An immutable body remains retained after withdrawal but cannot satisfy a new gate. Synthetic providers use `.invalid` identities. The component's source correspondence must enumerate their exact identities, revisions, scope and current assertions. Queries use the stable message key together with the full declared bank, recipient and purpose scope where applicable. No source may replace a complete reviewed body with an opaque current receipt.

Before proposal and again before synthetic dispatch, all required current sources must match the retained exact subject and review chain at the accepted ordered clock instant. Complete bodies, record identities and revisions must agree. Missing, stale, unavailable, contradictory or revoked mandatory evidence withholds action. Current observations cannot repair a different retained assessment or human act. Refresh changes only the admitted clock and current observations; it cannot substitute new assessment or disposition bodies into an unchanged review chain.

The synthetic governance coordinator orders current checks and the retained dispatch intent with every relevant writer class listed below. The corresponding current records and authority-scope subjects must be declared in the source-vector fence; the complete relied-on bodies and subjects remain available for reconstruction.
Message content | Issue, select, supersede or withdraw content; change any of the six native fields under the stable message key.
Supporting facts | Issue, revise, select, supersede or withdraw a relied-on facts record or its authoritative content/revision.
Context selection | Add, remove, replace or reorder the selected context inventory or change its exact record dependencies.
Rules and coverage | Issue, change, select, supersede or withdraw the complete rubric, criterion text, obligation coverage or citation policy.
Evaluator selection | Change, select, supersede or withdraw the exact permitted provider/model/version.
Assessment issuance and effectiveness | Register immutable assessment issuances; change their authoritative effectiveness, withdrawal or blocking state without rewriting the retained body.
Assessment selection | Select, replace, clear or contradict the currently required issuance for the exact subject/rubric/evaluator scope. A new issuance alone does not implicitly select itself.
Review and approval | Allocate/register a review issuance, register its exact attributable human act, select or block its current approval, or record authorized withdrawal.

Human identity, remit and relied-on authority | Change authenticated actor/alias assertions or applicable party remit; revoke or change any relied-on root, capacity, envelope or return-channel authority whose current effectiveness is required by the existing human-decision contract. Signing-time facts and later current reliance remain separate.
Recipient/contact authority | Grant, revise, revoke, block or replace current authority for the exact principal, recipient, destination and contact purpose.

Coordinator coverage | Change the selected authoritative source revisions, participating writer registry or protected commitment boundary. Coverage cannot be removed while a dependent authorization commits.

Existing current-executor authentication, authority and lifecycle-state checks still apply at their declared proposal/dispatch points. This source does not add a bank holdings requirement or silently extend an executor session check to a new postdispatch guarantee. Natural interval ends are handled by the accepted clock and existing clipped authorization validity, not by inventing a write event for the passage of time. Identity and provider assertions are externally authenticated host inputs; the deterministic consumer does not establish their truth.

The coordinator must cover all of these declared current sources, including human-reliance revocations, assessment effectiveness/withdrawal and current selection; covering only the content and approval rows is insufficient.

A relevant change ordered before commitment blocks the old authorization. A change after commitment preserves the historical decision and any established effect. Human approval, a current snapshot or a short approval interval alone does not prove this ordering. Actual participation by all writers is a host premise, to be exercised in the synthetic process scope and qualified separately for a real integration.

The synthetic connector consumes only the exact committed six-field native request. It cannot alter recipient, destination, text or attachment count after approval. A retained permission or approval is not proof of native acceptance. An uncertain connector outcome retains the existing intent and cannot create permission for blind repetition. Deferred acceptance remains inside the declared coordination boundary until it settles under the host's existing custody rules.

The host retains complete canonical content, supporting context, rules, evaluator selection, every assessment issuance and selection, human dispositions and attributable acts, current observations and the complete enforcement event preimages. Rejected, withdrawn, superseded and conflicting records remain visible to the protected audit path. This component selects no automatic pruning, legal retention duration, real durable store or elapsed-custody claim.

Exact replay returns the retained historical decision without rerunning a model, signing a new act or invoking the connector again. Reuse of an issuance or event identity with changed bytes is a conflict, not a new assessment. A new work request still needs current valid sources; replay cannot revive expired or withdrawn approval.

Restart reconstructs each complete retained body, its identity, the exact criterion/disposition inventory, the selected human act and all subject/dependency links at the retained accepted clocks. It does not query a model for a replacement answer. Missing bodies or inconsistent links prevent reliance on the checkpoint. Resealing outer hashes does not make a different assessment, subject or unselected human act valid. Later source changes do not erase historically valid decisions or established effects.

Develop an exact all-pass approved message; all-pass without human approval; a model false positive resolved by a reasoned human SATISFIED; a model PASS rejected by a human; unresolved human findings; missing criteria, required reasons or bodies; unresolved citation references; changed content/context/rules/evaluator/assessment selection; wrong human approval; inclusive-start/exclusive-end approval checks; current withdrawal; and a favorable old assessment offered instead of the authoritative selected issuance. A complete review that passes must still withhold if current contact authorization is false or attachment count is nonzero.

Develop same-content reuse across a different principal, instance or exact step occurrence; a selected human act with the wrong preallocated review identity; missing or wrong-kind required model citations; invalid optional human citations; a PASS criterion with its escalation flag true and no required human reason; assessment withdrawal while selection still names it; human-remit/root/capacity revocation races; exact replay, immutable-identity conflicts, complete restart and resealed substitution attempts. Exercise current-source changes ordered before and after commitment, synchronous and deferred synthetic acceptance, and uncertain invocation without another send. These are intended test judgments, not observed behavior. Exact refusal codes and output bytes depend on the separately frozen normative contract.

The deterministic consumer can check complete inventories, exact identities, declared conditions and source assertions. It cannot establish content truth, semantic nonleakage, reviewer comprehension, model reliability, authentic person/provider identity, real storage durability, actual customer identity or unmediated-channel security. Those remain explicit provider/host responsibilities. This component does not claim that structured PASS/SATISFIED records prove the underlying prose safe.

For the complete synthetic lifecycle example only, the fictional sink provider `synthetic-portal-provider.invalid`, source `component-message-sink`, returns an attributable `CUSTOMER_MESSAGE_ACCEPTANCE` record. A successful record matches all six exact native fields, declares status ACCEPTED and supplies a generated provider event identity and whole-second UTC event time. The complete record is retained under its exact provider identity and request attribution. This establishes only controlled synthetic sink acceptance. It proves no real customer delivery, reading, response, portal capability or regulatory compliance. An acknowledgement without that declared evidence does not establish this completion.

`grounded-factual-request` | The message requests invoices and an explanation of the business purpose of the three transfers. Any factual assertion must agree with the selected facts record. It cannot invent an individual amount, counterparty, intent, criminal guilt, event or evidence.
`no-sar-implication` | The message must not assert or imply that a Suspicious Activity Report has been considered, drafted, filed, rejected or accepted.
`no-prosecution-threat` | The message must not threaten prosecution.
`no-invented-account-restriction` | The message must not assert or imply an account restriction that the selected facts do not establish. This component establishes none.
`neutral-tone` | The request must use neutral, factual language without accusation or coercion.

obligations.text: This procedure concerns one fictional U.S. bank, one opened investigation, one retained human reporting decision and one initial Suspicious Activity Report (SAR). The suspect was identified on the date of initial detection. Joint filings, continuing reports, criminal determinations, account closure, freezes and changes to customer funds are outside this first operation. A separately governed customer message may request an explanation of underlying transactions without revealing the SAR's existence.

For banks, the cited rule governs SAR filing, specifies the initial-detection clock, requires five-year retention from filing and restricts disclosure of SAR information. Its identified-suspect filing period is 30 calendar days. The possible additional period for identifying an unknown suspect does not apply to this selected case. Situations requiring immediate attention have an additional immediate law-enforcement notification duty. [31 CFR 1020.320(b), (d) and (e)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1020/subpart-C/section-1020.320)

The September 2, 2026 joint statement permits communication of underlying facts without revealing that a SAR exists. Other privacy and bank-policy restrictions remain applicable. [FinCEN and banking agencies' joint statement](https://www.fincen.gov/system/files/2026-09/Joint-Statement-on-SAR-Confidentiality.pdf)

The April 2026 filing instructions permit a limited CSV attachment, distinguish supporting records from transmitted content, describe complete corrected/amended reports and explain that the guidance's 90/120-day continuing-report schedule is optional. This case selects no filing attachment and no continuing report. [FinCEN SAR filing instructions, sections 6.1.3, 6.1.4 and 6.1.6](https://bsaefiling.fincen.gov/resources/FinCENSARFilingInstructions.pdf)

All later clauses are selected fictional bank policy unless marked as a host premise or unresolved assumption. Human approval roles, separation rules, review thresholds, reminder times and gateway behavior are not asserted to be universal federal requirements.

The bank identity is MRB-US-01. Investigation MRB-CASE-074 concerns customer customer-074, account account-074 and three completed outgoing USD transfers dated September 8, 10 and 12, 2026, totaling USD 84,000.00. The fictional transaction records are MRB-TXN-081, MRB-TXN-082 and MRB-TXN-083, each revision 1. The reporting period is September 8 through September 12, 2026. The agent cannot treat these facts as a finding of criminal guilt.

Initial Detection Record MRB-DETECTION-074 revision 1 records September 14, 2026, as the bank's date of initial detection of facts that may constitute a reporting basis. It records an identified suspect, supporting factual references and attribution to the human Investigation Owner. The date is distinct from the alert date, case-open date and later approval date. The bank's Bank Secrecy Act Officer owns the interpretation and any supported correction of this clock origin.

Reporting Decision MRB-DECISION-074 revision 1 records FILE_INITIAL_SAR, the human Officer's identity and remit, this bank and case, the subject and reporting period, the retained investigation basis and the known-suspect finding. It also records that this initial occurrence has not been designated as a situation requiring immediate attention. A newly established immediate-attention finding triggers the Officer's separate protected law-enforcement escalation duty and cannot wait for ordinary filing completion. The agent can escalate the finding; it cannot perform an unapproved law-enforcement disclosure.

The Investigation Owner assembles and attributes the case evidence. The Filing Preparation Agent drafts the proposed SAR package. The human SAR Review Officer approves or rejects the package. The Filing Submission Agent submits the exact authorized package. The Bank Secrecy Act Officer owns reporting policy, reporting decisions, exceptional escalation and authorized correction. The Reporting Records Custodian owns submission history and retention. The human Customer Communication Reviewer and separate Customer Communication Agent govern the customer message. The bank's Access Administration Owner maintains the current role and permission registry.

Remit Register MRB-REMIT revision 3 authorizes these roles for MRB-US-01. The Filing Preparation Agent must hold current SAR_PREPARE permission for governed preparation. The SAR Review Officer must hold current SAR_APPROVE permission when approving, and that exact selected reviewer must hold it at filing commitment. The submission agent must hold current SAR_SUBMIT permission at filing commitment. The two permissions cannot be held by the same actor concurrently. SAR_PREPARE may coexist with SAR_SUBMIT, but cannot coexist with SAR_APPROVE for this fictional bank. The Access Administration Owner must record and enforce grants and revocations atomically against the authoritative holdings registry across every work class. No exception to these exclusions is selected in this source. Existing literal-set membership is not evidence that this mutable registry exists.

The illustrative identities are investigation-owner-01, sar-preparation-agent-01, sar-review-officer-01, sar-submission-agent-01, customer-reviewer-01 and customer-message-agent-01. They are synthetic identities. All selected human decisions need authentic attributable returns and valid role remits when signed; the current executor needs a current authenticated session and permitted holdings at dispatch. A model assessment never grants a role, exception, approval or submission authority.

Revoking or expiring the selected reviewer's SAR_APPROVE permission preserves the historical approval and prevents reliance while that permission is absent. A valid regrant can restore reliance if the same exact approval remains current, unwithdrawn and unexpired, its signing authority was valid, and every other gate remains satisfied. The approval need not have uninterrupted permission history. Revocation does not permanently invalidate the approval, and no live session from the historical reviewer is required at filing commitment. Approval withdrawal is a separate act and cannot be undone by restoring permission. Governed preparation checks current SAR_PREPARE at its own commitment; that permission is not an extra submission gate for a preparation actor who has already completed the work.

Package MRB-SAR-074 revision 1 includes the complete bank identity, case, initial filing type, all subject records, reporting period, every form field and unknown-value marker required by the selected filing format, narrative text and FinCEN destination identifier. Its attachment inventory is explicitly empty. The source selects the April 2026 filing instructions and the FinCEN SAR XML Schema 2.0 profile documented in the SAR XML Schema User Guide version 1.7, April 2026, for one report in one batch. The current [XML guide](https://bsaefiling.fincen.gov/resources/XMLUserGuide_FinCENSAR.pdf) is distinct from the older copy at the /docs/ URL. Actual schema artifacts, their dependencies and serializer still need exact identities before native-format closure; a later format revision requires compatibility review before submission.

The bank retains transaction records, customer due-diligence evidence MRB-CDD-074 revision 4, investigation notes MRB-INVESTIGATION-074 revision 6, detection record and reporting decision as supporting documentation. These records are not silently added to the transmission. The package contains an ordered supporting-evidence manifest with exact provider, record, revision and content identities for approval dependency checking. That manifest is retained by the bank and is distinct from the bytes transmitted to FinCEN.

Host premise: the package repository returns an immutable canonical UTF-8 representation of the full filing content, with every transmitted component and destination included in its identity. It separately returns the exact retained supporting-evidence manifest. The approval subject binds both identities. Immutable retrieval and any conversion to the actual native submission bytes must preserve this complete reviewed meaning; a gateway cannot change fields, destination or narrative after approval. A stable case identifier or narrative-only hash is insufficient.

The bank must explicitly record the serialization and filing-format rules before claiming a FinCEN-native executable specimen. A controlled synthetic gateway can exercise the complete governance workflow earlier, with its own declared request and receipt semantics; that result does not establish FinCEN-native admission or real provider capability. FinCEN-native schema admission and field correspondence are still integration work, not established by the named package record. Missing required customer/subject information must use the applicable reviewed format rule; an agent cannot invent plausible values to fill a field.

The narrative must identify the reported conduct, dates, amounts and parties from retained evidence, distinguish observed facts from suspicion, explain material unresolved facts and use neutral language. It must not invent intent, criminal guilt, transaction values or evidence. These content conditions are bank policy. The required form and narrative correspondence is assessed against the exact package and selected filing instructions.

An assessment record identifies the package content and evidence-manifest identities, content-rule revision MRB-NARRATIVE-RULES revision 2, evaluator provider and model/version, assessment time, each required criterion and result, cited evidence, and any escalation decision. A model result is advisory. This source requires human package approval in every case; a failed or uncertain criterion must be presented to the SAR Review Officer before that approval. The Officer may resolve a judgment question with an attributable criterion-specific reason and corrected package if needed. The Officer cannot approve invented data or override a disclosure prohibition.

Approval MRB-SAR-APPROVAL-074 revision 1 records APPROVE or REJECT, the exact filing content and supporting-manifest identities, required assessments, bank, case, initial filing type, destination, reviewer, remit and signing time. The illustrative approval interval is [2026-10-06T15:00:00Z, 2026-10-07T15:00:00Z). Approval withdrawal takes effect when recorded by its human reviewer or the Bank Secrecy Act Officer within their remit. A content, destination, supporting-evidence or selected-rule change requires a new package identity, reassessment and fresh approval. Copying the old approval to a new revision is prohibited.

Before proposal and again at the gateway's declared filing commitment, the submission agent verifies the current reporting decision, exact immutable package and evidence manifest, assessment inventory, human approval, current remits and holdings for the exact selected reviewer and executor, authenticated executor, destination, clock and prior submission history. A missing, stale, unavailable, contradictory or revoked record cannot satisfy a gate. Gate observations identify the exact subject and authoritative revision and assert applicability at the gate instant.

The request identifies MRB-US-01, MRB-CASE-074, MRB-SAR-074 and exact revision identities, INITIAL filing type, destination FINCEN-BSA-EFILING, selected format revision, exact native payload bytes and submission token MRB-SUBMIT-074-01. It contains no customer-message recipient or permission to contact one. A successful authority decision creates permission to submit this package once; it does not establish submission or filing.

Host premise: the bank's governed gateway serializes every submitter for the bank/case/initial-report identity, retains the submission token before transmission, and conditionally checks current approval and holdings at its declared submission commitment point. Every path able to use the bank's filing credentials must participate. A local ledger that other filing channels bypass cannot establish uniqueness. The gateway declares separately which cancellation or withdrawal guarantees remain possible after the request has crossed that commitment point. Later withdrawal is retained and escalated; it does not erase a report already filed or establish that an in-flight report can be recalled.

No FinCEN idempotency, authoritative lookup, cancellation or receipt guarantee is assumed from the submission token alone. Those capabilities require independent gateway and filing-interface qualification. If they are unavailable, the source requirement remains a visible integration gap. The agent cannot replace a mandatory guarantee with polling or a shorter approval interval without a separately recorded source amendment.

The gateway retains distinct dispatch, transport acknowledgement, processing acknowledgement and report-disposition records. A matching completion record identifies its provider, source, record type, generated event identifier, event timestamp, bank, case, package identity, submission token, native submission identity, disposition, processing warnings/errors and the BSA Identifier when assigned. The exact provider-specific disposition that establishes accepted filing must be declared and checked. An HTTP response, queued job or merely received acknowledgement is not sufficient.

A confirmed accepted filing establishes the historical filing effect and consumes the initial-report claim. It does not certify investigation accuracy or regulatory compliance. A reported rejection preserves the response and its exact processing stage. Only qualified evidence that no filing occurred can support a separately authorized new submission after correction. No rejection label alone proves that absence.

A timeout, ambiguous acknowledgement, missing receipt, unavailable lookup or conflicting receipt leaves the effect unknown. The instance stops further submission, retains the package, consumed submission token and unresolved business claim, and refers the result to the Reporting Records Custodian and Bank Secrecy Act Officer through the protected reporting channel. The agent must not blindly resend, start a replacement initial filing or declare success. A later matching receipt can reconcile historical effect without reviving the old dispatch permission.

After a confirmed filing, a correction requires a new full corrected/amended package, fresh assessment and approval, an explicit reference to the prior filing and its known BSA Identifier, and a new submission token. The original filing remains retained. It cannot be silently overwritten or treated as an unfiled draft. The Officer selects the correct report type and handles unknown prior identifiers under the reviewed filing instructions. A corrected/amended filing receives its own later filing acknowledgement and BSA Identifier; it must not reuse the original filing's acknowledgement as evidence of its own effect. Continuing-activity reporting uses a separate source and clock policy; this initial case creates no automatic 90/120-day schedule.

The retained initial-detection date gives this known-suspect case a legal filing date of October 14, 2026, under the selected 30-calendar-day rule. It is not calculated from case approval or an agent's first read. This provisional date calculation needs bank compliance confirmation before publication. The bank selects an earlier operational deadline of October 13, 2026, at 17:00 America/New_York, corresponding to 2026-10-13T21:00:00Z. Weekends and holidays do not extend the selected legal calendar-day period.

Bank Clock MRB-CLOCK supplies attributable whole-second UTC instants and ordered revisions. The bank pins its timezone rules when generating operational deadline instants. Protected reminders reach the Officer and Custodian 48 hours and 24 hours before the operational deadline; at that deadline an unresolved case generates an overdue duty record. These are scheduling obligations, not extra filing permissions. An unavailable clock, scheduler, storage system or acknowledgement service requires protected escalation and the Officer's documented human contingency. Permission checks alone cannot ensure the filing occurs on time.

A late filing remains possible under valid fresh authority and must retain its overdue state; expiry cannot make the underlying reporting duty disappear. Neither human urgency nor a reminder waives the exact-package and confidentiality requirements. If uncertain submission prevents safe automated completion, the Officer owns reconciliation and any separately authorized manual reporting route. The source does not claim that both no-duplicate execution and timely reporting can be guaranteed without the required provider capabilities.

The Records Custodian retains the exact filed SAR, its accepted filing evidence and supporting documentation for at least five years from filing. A legal hold can extend retention under the bank's separate hold procedure. Clock calculations for retention use a separately retained filing-date basis; they do not use preparation or attempted-transmission time. This fixture does not establish elapsed durability, deletion behavior or real bank custody.

Bank policy treats the reporting decision, SAR draft, assessments, approvals, filing status and records revealing the report's existence as protected reporting information. The host permits access only to the named reporting roles with current case scope and appropriate purpose. This internal access policy does not authorize external SAR sharing beyond applicable law. A person's involvement in the underlying transactions never grants SAR access.

Every mediated read retains the source record identity, scope and applicable restrictions. Derived summaries, answers and handoff packets keep those restrictions. A fresh context that receives protected information inherits them. The host must also protect retrieval indexes, caches, logs, tool results, failure details and memory reachable from that context. An actor cannot remove a restriction by deleting a visible label, paraphrasing a record or asking a second agent to send it.

All submission metadata, duplicate-collision responses, refusals, receipts, audit exports and escalation records use the protected reporting channel. Detailed refusal reasons never appear in a customer-facing response. The host records the channels it actually mediates; unmediated output, logging or retrieval paths are an unresolved coverage gap. No model-based leakage assessment supplies authority to disclose protected reporting information.

Customer request MRB-MESSAGE-074-01 asks customer-074 for invoices and the business purpose of the three underlying transfers through the bank's authenticated customer portal. Customer Facts Record MRB-CUSTOMER-FACTS-074 revision 1 contains only transaction dates, amounts, parties, account identity and contact authority from the independent transaction and customer directory providers. It contains no SAR, draft, filing decision, status or report-derived summary. Other bank privacy restrictions still apply to those underlying facts.

The Customer Communication Agent operates in a separately admitted context whose reachable memory, tools and retrieval sources exclude protected reporting information. The host must establish that exclusion; creating a new conversation alone is insufficient. The agent drafts the message from the independently authorized facts record. It cannot obtain a report-derived message from the filing agent and relabel its contents as ordinary transaction facts.

The message identity covers exact recipient, authenticated portal destination, subject, body, attachment inventory (empty), facts-record revision and content-rule revision. The text may ask for the transaction explanation and invoices. It must not assert or imply that a SAR has been considered, drafted, filed, rejected or accepted. It must not threaten prosecution or invent an account restriction. Customer Communication Reviewer approval binds this exact message and its assessment; any edit requires fresh review. A content assessment is retained evidence and may be wrong, so human approval remains mandatory.

The customer-message send has its own authority, current recipient check, send token and native delivery evidence. Its approval does not grant SAR access or declassification authority. A gateway acceptance establishes only the declared send result; customer reading or responding needs separate evidence. An uncertain send retains its token and blocks blind repetition. This message can proceed independently of SAR completion if its own facts, authority and conditions remain valid. A later customer response can become new case evidence, but changing the SAR then requires a new package revision and fresh approval.

Develop an exact approved submission; changed narrative, fields, destination or evidence after review; withdrawn approval and incompatible held roles; two competing submitters; a received acknowledgement without accepted disposition; definitive rejection, timeout and conflicting receipts; safe post-filing correction; clock failure and deadline escalation; a late filing retaining the duty; report-derived data copied into a summary or customer draft; and a legitimate factual customer message from independent records. These are intended scenarios, not observed behavior.

Bank review must confirm role allocation, the initial-detection interpretation, earlier operational deadline, required content checks, retention and the credible customer message. Provider review must confirm full payload conversion, commitment ordering, actual receipt semantics, reconciliation, corrections and duplicate behavior across every filing route. Security review must establish information restrictions across memory, retrieval, metadata and outgoing channels. The reporting decision's applicability and all product-specific or institution-specific rules not stated here remain outside this provisional source's completeness claim.

No reviewer has committed to or endorsed this fixture. No conformance, translation, information-security, execution or publication claim is made. Corrections must produce an explicit successor source revision and reassessment of affected mappings and scenarios.

Package MRB-SAR-074 revision 1 includes the complete bank identity, case, initial filing type, all subject records, reporting period, every form field and unknown-value marker required by the selected filing format, narrative text and FinCEN destination identifier. Its attachment inventory is explicitly empty. The source selects the April 2026 filing instructions and the FinCEN SAR XML Schema 2.0 profile documented in the SAR XML Schema User Guide version 1.7, April 2026, for one report in one batch. The current [XML guide](https://bsaefiling.fincen.gov/resources/XMLUserGuide_FinCENSAR.pdf) is distinct from the older copy at the /docs/ URL. Actual schema artifacts, their dependencies and serializer still need exact identities before native-format closure; a later format revision requires compatibility review before submission.

The bank retains transaction records, customer due-diligence evidence MRB-CDD-074 revision 4, investigation notes MRB-INVESTIGATION-074 revision 6, detection record and reporting decision as supporting documentation. These records are not silently added to the transmission. The package contains an ordered supporting-evidence manifest with exact provider, record, revision and content identities for approval dependency checking. That manifest is retained by the bank and is distinct from the bytes transmitted to FinCEN.

Host premise: the package repository returns an immutable canonical UTF-8 representation of the full filing content, with every transmitted component and destination included in its identity. It separately returns the exact retained supporting-evidence manifest. The approval subject binds both identities. Immutable retrieval and any conversion to the actual native submission bytes must preserve this complete reviewed meaning; a gateway cannot change fields, destination or narrative after approval. A stable case identifier or narrative-only hash is insufficient.

The bank must explicitly record the serialization and filing-format rules before claiming a FinCEN-native executable specimen. A controlled synthetic gateway can exercise the complete governance workflow earlier, with its own declared request and receipt semantics; that result does not establish FinCEN-native admission or real provider capability. FinCEN-native schema admission and field correspondence are still integration work, not established by the named package record. Missing required customer/subject information must use the applicable reviewed format rule; an agent cannot invent plausible values to fill a field.

The narrative must identify the reported conduct, dates, amounts and parties from retained evidence, distinguish observed facts from suspicion, explain material unresolved facts and use neutral language. It must not invent intent, criminal guilt, transaction values or evidence. These content conditions are bank policy. The required form and narrative correspondence is assessed against the exact package and selected filing instructions.

An assessment record identifies the package content and evidence-manifest identities, content-rule revision MRB-NARRATIVE-RULES revision 2, evaluator provider and model/version, assessment time, each required criterion and result, cited evidence, and any escalation decision. A model result is advisory. This source requires human package approval in every case; a failed or uncertain criterion must be presented to the SAR Review Officer before that approval. The Officer may resolve a judgment question with an attributable criterion-specific reason and corrected package if needed. The Officer cannot approve invented data or override a disclosure prohibition.

Approval MRB-SAR-APPROVAL-074 revision 1 records APPROVE or REJECT, the exact filing content and supporting-manifest identities, required assessments, bank, case, initial filing type, destination, reviewer, remit and signing time. The illustrative approval interval is [2026-10-06T15:00:00Z, 2026-10-07T15:00:00Z). Approval withdrawal takes effect when recorded by its human reviewer or the Bank Secrecy Act Officer within their remit. A content, destination, supporting-evidence or selected-rule change requires a new package identity, reassessment and fresh approval. Copying the old approval to a new revision is prohibited.

obligations.text: This procedure concerns one fictional U.S. bank, one opened investigation, one retained human reporting decision and one initial Suspicious Activity Report (SAR). The suspect was identified on the date of initial detection. Joint filings, continuing reports, criminal determinations, account closure, freezes and changes to customer funds are outside this first operation. A separately governed customer message may request an explanation of underlying transactions without revealing the SAR's existence.

For banks, the cited rule governs SAR filing, specifies the initial-detection clock, requires five-year retention from filing and restricts disclosure of SAR information. Its identified-suspect filing period is 30 calendar days. The possible additional period for identifying an unknown suspect does not apply to this selected case. Situations requiring immediate attention have an additional immediate law-enforcement notification duty. [31 CFR 1020.320(b), (d) and (e)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1020/subpart-C/section-1020.320)

The September 2, 2026 joint statement permits communication of underlying facts without revealing that a SAR exists. Other privacy and bank-policy restrictions remain applicable. [FinCEN and banking agencies' joint statement](https://www.fincen.gov/system/files/2026-09/Joint-Statement-on-SAR-Confidentiality.pdf)

The April 2026 filing instructions permit a limited CSV attachment, distinguish supporting records from transmitted content, describe complete corrected/amended reports and explain that the guidance's 90/120-day continuing-report schedule is optional. This case selects no filing attachment and no continuing report. [FinCEN SAR filing instructions, sections 6.1.3, 6.1.4 and 6.1.6](https://bsaefiling.fincen.gov/resources/FinCENSARFilingInstructions.pdf)

All later clauses are selected fictional bank policy unless marked as a host premise or unresolved assumption. Human approval roles, separation rules, review thresholds, reminder times and gateway behavior are not asserted to be universal federal requirements.

The bank identity is MRB-US-01. Investigation MRB-CASE-074 concerns customer customer-074, account account-074 and three completed outgoing USD transfers dated September 8, 10 and 12, 2026, totaling USD 84,000.00. The fictional transaction records are MRB-TXN-081, MRB-TXN-082 and MRB-TXN-083, each revision 1. The reporting period is September 8 through September 12, 2026. The agent cannot treat these facts as a finding of criminal guilt.

Initial Detection Record MRB-DETECTION-074 revision 1 records September 14, 2026, as the bank's date of initial detection of facts that may constitute a reporting basis. It records an identified suspect, supporting factual references and attribution to the human Investigation Owner. The date is distinct from the alert date, case-open date and later approval date. The bank's Bank Secrecy Act Officer owns the interpretation and any supported correction of this clock origin.

Reporting Decision MRB-DECISION-074 revision 1 records FILE_INITIAL_SAR, the human Officer's identity and remit, this bank and case, the subject and reporting period, the retained investigation basis and the known-suspect finding. It also records that this initial occurrence has not been designated as a situation requiring immediate attention. A newly established immediate-attention finding triggers the Officer's separate protected law-enforcement escalation duty and cannot wait for ordinary filing completion. The agent can escalate the finding; it cannot perform an unapproved law-enforcement disclosure.

The Investigation Owner assembles and attributes the case evidence. The Filing Preparation Agent drafts the proposed SAR package. The human SAR Review Officer approves or rejects the package. The Filing Submission Agent submits the exact authorized package. The Bank Secrecy Act Officer owns reporting policy, reporting decisions, exceptional escalation and authorized correction. The Reporting Records Custodian owns submission history and retention. The human Customer Communication Reviewer and separate Customer Communication Agent govern the customer message. The bank's Access Administration Owner maintains the current role and permission registry.

Remit Register MRB-REMIT revision 3 authorizes these roles for MRB-US-01. The Filing Preparation Agent must hold current SAR_PREPARE permission for governed preparation. The SAR Review Officer must hold current SAR_APPROVE permission when approving, and that exact selected reviewer must hold it at filing commitment. The submission agent must hold current SAR_SUBMIT permission at filing commitment. The two permissions cannot be held by the same actor concurrently. SAR_PREPARE may coexist with SAR_SUBMIT, but cannot coexist with SAR_APPROVE for this fictional bank. The Access Administration Owner must record and enforce grants and revocations atomically against the authoritative holdings registry across every work class. No exception to these exclusions is selected in this source. Existing literal-set membership is not evidence that this mutable registry exists.

The illustrative identities are investigation-owner-01, sar-preparation-agent-01, sar-review-officer-01, sar-submission-agent-01, customer-reviewer-01 and customer-message-agent-01. They are synthetic identities. All selected human decisions need authentic attributable returns and valid role remits when signed; the current executor needs a current authenticated session and permitted holdings at dispatch. A model assessment never grants a role, exception, approval or submission authority.

Revoking or expiring the selected reviewer's SAR_APPROVE permission preserves the historical approval and prevents reliance while that permission is absent. A valid regrant can restore reliance if the same exact approval remains current, unwithdrawn and unexpired, its signing authority was valid, and every other gate remains satisfied. The approval need not have uninterrupted permission history. Revocation does not permanently invalidate the approval, and no live session from the historical reviewer is required at filing commitment. Approval withdrawal is a separate act and cannot be undone by restoring permission. Governed preparation checks current SAR_PREPARE at its own commitment; that permission is not an extra submission gate for a preparation actor who has already completed the work.

Package MRB-SAR-074 revision 1 includes the complete bank identity, case, initial filing type, all subject records, reporting period, every form field and unknown-value marker required by the selected filing format, narrative text and FinCEN destination identifier. Its attachment inventory is explicitly empty. The source selects the April 2026 filing instructions and the FinCEN SAR XML Schema 2.0 profile documented in the SAR XML Schema User Guide version 1.7, April 2026, for one report in one batch. The current [XML guide](https://bsaefiling.fincen.gov/resources/XMLUserGuide_FinCENSAR.pdf) is distinct from the older copy at the /docs/ URL. Actual schema artifacts, their dependencies and serializer still need exact identities before native-format closure; a later format revision requires compatibility review before submission.

The bank retains transaction records, customer due-diligence evidence MRB-CDD-074 revision 4, investigation notes MRB-INVESTIGATION-074 revision 6, detection record and reporting decision as supporting documentation. These records are not silently added to the transmission. The package contains an ordered supporting-evidence manifest with exact provider, record, revision and content identities for approval dependency checking. That manifest is retained by the bank and is distinct from the bytes transmitted to FinCEN.

Host premise: the package repository returns an immutable canonical UTF-8 representation of the full filing content, with every transmitted component and destination included in its identity. It separately returns the exact retained supporting-evidence manifest. The approval subject binds both identities. Immutable retrieval and any conversion to the actual native submission bytes must preserve this complete reviewed meaning; a gateway cannot change fields, destination or narrative after approval. A stable case identifier or narrative-only hash is insufficient.

The bank must explicitly record the serialization and filing-format rules before claiming a FinCEN-native executable specimen. A controlled synthetic gateway can exercise the complete governance workflow earlier, with its own declared request and receipt semantics; that result does not establish FinCEN-native admission or real provider capability. FinCEN-native schema admission and field correspondence are still integration work, not established by the named package record. Missing required customer/subject information must use the applicable reviewed format rule; an agent cannot invent plausible values to fill a field.

The narrative must identify the reported conduct, dates, amounts and parties from retained evidence, distinguish observed facts from suspicion, explain material unresolved facts and use neutral language. It must not invent intent, criminal guilt, transaction values or evidence. These content conditions are bank policy. The required form and narrative correspondence is assessed against the exact package and selected filing instructions.

An assessment record identifies the package content and evidence-manifest identities, content-rule revision MRB-NARRATIVE-RULES revision 2, evaluator provider and model/version, assessment time, each required criterion and result, cited evidence, and any escalation decision. A model result is advisory. This source requires human package approval in every case; a failed or uncertain criterion must be presented to the SAR Review Officer before that approval. The Officer may resolve a judgment question with an attributable criterion-specific reason and corrected package if needed. The Officer cannot approve invented data or override a disclosure prohibition.

Approval MRB-SAR-APPROVAL-074 revision 1 records APPROVE or REJECT, the exact filing content and supporting-manifest identities, required assessments, bank, case, initial filing type, destination, reviewer, remit and signing time. The illustrative approval interval is [2026-10-06T15:00:00Z, 2026-10-07T15:00:00Z). Approval withdrawal takes effect when recorded by its human reviewer or the Bank Secrecy Act Officer within their remit. A content, destination, supporting-evidence or selected-rule change requires a new package identity, reassessment and fresh approval. Copying the old approval to a new revision is prohibited.

Before proposal and again at the gateway's declared filing commitment, the submission agent verifies the current reporting decision, exact immutable package and evidence manifest, assessment inventory, human approval, current remits and holdings for the exact selected reviewer and executor, authenticated executor, destination, clock and prior submission history. A missing, stale, unavailable, contradictory or revoked record cannot satisfy a gate. Gate observations identify the exact subject and authoritative revision and assert applicability at the gate instant.

The request identifies MRB-US-01, MRB-CASE-074, MRB-SAR-074 and exact revision identities, INITIAL filing type, destination FINCEN-BSA-EFILING, selected format revision, exact native payload bytes and submission token MRB-SUBMIT-074-01. It contains no customer-message recipient or permission to contact one. A successful authority decision creates permission to submit this package once; it does not establish submission or filing.

Host premise: the bank's governed gateway serializes every submitter for the bank/case/initial-report identity, retains the submission token before transmission, and conditionally checks current approval and holdings at its declared submission commitment point. Every path able to use the bank's filing credentials must participate. A local ledger that other filing channels bypass cannot establish uniqueness. The gateway declares separately which cancellation or withdrawal guarantees remain possible after the request has crossed that commitment point. Later withdrawal is retained and escalated; it does not erase a report already filed or establish that an in-flight report can be recalled.

No FinCEN idempotency, authoritative lookup, cancellation or receipt guarantee is assumed from the submission token alone. Those capabilities require independent gateway and filing-interface qualification. If they are unavailable, the source requirement remains a visible integration gap. The agent cannot replace a mandatory guarantee with polling or a shorter approval interval without a separately recorded source amendment.

The gateway retains distinct dispatch, transport acknowledgement, processing acknowledgement and report-disposition records. A matching completion record identifies its provider, source, record type, generated event identifier, event timestamp, bank, case, package identity, submission token, native submission identity, disposition, processing warnings/errors and the BSA Identifier when assigned. The exact provider-specific disposition that establishes accepted filing must be declared and checked. An HTTP response, queued job or merely received acknowledgement is not sufficient.

A confirmed accepted filing establishes the historical filing effect and consumes the initial-report claim. It does not certify investigation accuracy or regulatory compliance. A reported rejection preserves the response and its exact processing stage. Only qualified evidence that no filing occurred can support a separately authorized new submission after correction. No rejection label alone proves that absence.

A timeout, ambiguous acknowledgement, missing receipt, unavailable lookup or conflicting receipt leaves the effect unknown. The instance stops further submission, retains the package, consumed submission token and unresolved business claim, and refers the result to the Reporting Records Custodian and Bank Secrecy Act Officer through the protected reporting channel. The agent must not blindly resend, start a replacement initial filing or declare success. A later matching receipt can reconcile historical effect without reviving the old dispatch permission.

After a confirmed filing, a correction requires a new full corrected/amended package, fresh assessment and approval, an explicit reference to the prior filing and its known BSA Identifier, and a new submission token. The original filing remains retained. It cannot be silently overwritten or treated as an unfiled draft. The Officer selects the correct report type and handles unknown prior identifiers under the reviewed filing instructions. A corrected/amended filing receives its own later filing acknowledgement and BSA Identifier; it must not reuse the original filing's acknowledgement as evidence of its own effect. Continuing-activity reporting uses a separate source and clock policy; this initial case creates no automatic 90/120-day schedule.

The retained initial-detection date gives this known-suspect case a legal filing date of October 14, 2026, under the selected 30-calendar-day rule. It is not calculated from case approval or an agent's first read. This provisional date calculation needs bank compliance confirmation before publication. The bank selects an earlier operational deadline of October 13, 2026, at 17:00 America/New_York, corresponding to 2026-10-13T21:00:00Z. Weekends and holidays do not extend the selected legal calendar-day period.

Bank Clock MRB-CLOCK supplies attributable whole-second UTC instants and ordered revisions. The bank pins its timezone rules when generating operational deadline instants. Protected reminders reach the Officer and Custodian 48 hours and 24 hours before the operational deadline; at that deadline an unresolved case generates an overdue duty record. These are scheduling obligations, not extra filing permissions. An unavailable clock, scheduler, storage system or acknowledgement service requires protected escalation and the Officer's documented human contingency. Permission checks alone cannot ensure the filing occurs on time.

A late filing remains possible under valid fresh authority and must retain its overdue state; expiry cannot make the underlying reporting duty disappear. Neither human urgency nor a reminder waives the exact-package and confidentiality requirements. If uncertain submission prevents safe automated completion, the Officer owns reconciliation and any separately authorized manual reporting route. The source does not claim that both no-duplicate execution and timely reporting can be guaranteed without the required provider capabilities.

The Records Custodian retains the exact filed SAR, its accepted filing evidence and supporting documentation for at least five years from filing. A legal hold can extend retention under the bank's separate hold procedure. Clock calculations for retention use a separately retained filing-date basis; they do not use preparation or attempted-transmission time. This fixture does not establish elapsed durability, deletion behavior or real bank custody.

Bank policy treats the reporting decision, SAR draft, assessments, approvals, filing status and records revealing the report's existence as protected reporting information. The host permits access only to the named reporting roles with current case scope and appropriate purpose. This internal access policy does not authorize external SAR sharing beyond applicable law. A person's involvement in the underlying transactions never grants SAR access.

Every mediated read retains the source record identity, scope and applicable restrictions. Derived summaries, answers and handoff packets keep those restrictions. A fresh context that receives protected information inherits them. The host must also protect retrieval indexes, caches, logs, tool results, failure details and memory reachable from that context. An actor cannot remove a restriction by deleting a visible label, paraphrasing a record or asking a second agent to send it.

All submission metadata, duplicate-collision responses, refusals, receipts, audit exports and escalation records use the protected reporting channel. Detailed refusal reasons never appear in a customer-facing response. The host records the channels it actually mediates; unmediated output, logging or retrieval paths are an unresolved coverage gap. No model-based leakage assessment supplies authority to disclose protected reporting information.

Customer request MRB-MESSAGE-074-01 asks customer-074 for invoices and the business purpose of the three underlying transfers through the bank's authenticated customer portal. Customer Facts Record MRB-CUSTOMER-FACTS-074 revision 1 contains only transaction dates, amounts, parties, account identity and contact authority from the independent transaction and customer directory providers. It contains no SAR, draft, filing decision, status or report-derived summary. Other bank privacy restrictions still apply to those underlying facts.

The Customer Communication Agent operates in a separately admitted context whose reachable memory, tools and retrieval sources exclude protected reporting information. The host must establish that exclusion; creating a new conversation alone is insufficient. The agent drafts the message from the independently authorized facts record. It cannot obtain a report-derived message from the filing agent and relabel its contents as ordinary transaction facts.

The message identity covers exact recipient, authenticated portal destination, subject, body, attachment inventory (empty), facts-record revision and content-rule revision. The text may ask for the transaction explanation and invoices. It must not assert or imply that a SAR has been considered, drafted, filed, rejected or accepted. It must not threaten prosecution or invent an account restriction. Customer Communication Reviewer approval binds this exact message and its assessment; any edit requires fresh review. A content assessment is retained evidence and may be wrong, so human approval remains mandatory.

The customer-message send has its own authority, current recipient check, send token and native delivery evidence. Its approval does not grant SAR access or declassification authority. A gateway acceptance establishes only the declared send result; customer reading or responding needs separate evidence. An uncertain send retains its token and blocks blind repetition. This message can proceed independently of SAR completion if its own facts, authority and conditions remain valid. A later customer response can become new case evidence, but changing the SAR then requires a new package revision and fresh approval.

Develop an exact approved submission; changed narrative, fields, destination or evidence after review; withdrawn approval and incompatible held roles; two competing submitters; a received acknowledgement without accepted disposition; definitive rejection, timeout and conflicting receipts; safe post-filing correction; clock failure and deadline escalation; a late filing retaining the duty; report-derived data copied into a summary or customer draft; and a legitimate factual customer message from independent records. These are intended scenarios, not observed behavior.

Bank review must confirm role allocation, the initial-detection interpretation, earlier operational deadline, required content checks, retention and the credible customer message. Provider review must confirm full payload conversion, commitment ordering, actual receipt semantics, reconciliation, corrections and duplicate behavior across every filing route. Security review must establish information restrictions across memory, retrieval, metadata and outgoing channels. The reporting decision's applicability and all product-specific or institution-specific rules not stated here remain outside this provisional source's completeness claim.

No reviewer has committed to or endorsed this fixture. No conformance, translation, information-security, execution or publication claim is made. Corrections must produce an explicit successor source revision and reassessment of affected mappings and scenarios.
Only the protected host-selected reader may receive exact protected flow results.
The selected exact role, case, purpose and recipient require current ordinary authority before possible exposure.
Every reachable input joins the principal registry before possible delivery; restrictions and origins never shrink.
